Jaguar lead the teams' championship on 288 points, holding a slim advantage over Porsche. Mitch Evans is their strongest driver at third overall with 160 points, while António Félix Da Costa sits sixth on 128, leaving a clear gap between the two.

Porsche sit second on 271 points, just behind Jaguar. Pascal Wehrlein is a genuine title contender at the top of the drivers' standings with 169 points, while Nico Müller trails further back on 102, so most of the team's tally comes from one driver.

Mahindra are third on 252 points, comfortably clear of the midfield behind them. Edoardo Mortara leads the pair at fifth with 137 points and Nyck de Vries is close behind at seventh on 115, giving Mahindra a well balanced lineup.

Andretti are fourth on 229 points. Jake Dennis is their standout driver, sitting second overall with 164 points, while Felipe Drugovich sits much lower at fourteenth on 65, so the team's score rests heavily on its leading man.
Citroën are fifth on 182 points. Nick Cassidy leads their drivers at eighth with 114 points, while Jean-Éric Vergne sits twelfth on 68, leaving a noticeable gap between the two.

Nissan are sixth on 157 points. Oliver Rowland is their strongest at fourth overall with 137 points, whereas Norman Nato has struggled to score, finishing nineteenth with just 20 and leaving a wide margin between the pair.
Envision are seventh on 152 points. Sébastien Buemi leads at tenth with 97 points, while Joel Eriksson sits sixteenth on 55, so the team's points come largely from its more experienced driver.

Cupra Kiro are eighth on 128 points. Josep Maria Martí leads the pair at thirteenth with 66 points and Dan Ticktum is close behind at fifteenth on 62, making this one of the closest driver matchups in the field.
DS Penske are ninth on 91 points. Taylor Barnard leads at eleventh with 68 points, while Maximilian Günther sits eighteenth on 23, leaving a substantial gap between the two drivers.
